captions.linkedin:
I built an AI-powered email router in n8n that reads every new email in my Gmail inbox and automatically sorts it into five categories: work, learning, important (security alerts, payment confirmations), other, and "needs review."

It runs on its own every hour and scored 8/8 on real emails after testing.

The biggest lessons weren't about AI. They were about me. I had to clean the input, because it was also sorting my own sent emails. I had to clearly define what "important" means to me. And I had to fix the wiring when a new category shifted the outputs.

The takeaway: the hardest part of automation isn't the technology, it's defining the rules.

What repetitive task in your work would you automate first?
